correctness.rationale: Exact definitions and quantifiers are n>=2 and Omega(n)<=8. Four-layeredness implies sigma(n)>=4n. For each exponent a>=1, A_a(p)<p/(p-1), and replacing each new prime by the smallest admissible later prime yields a rigorous global upper envelope. Increasing-prime loops stop once the monotone next-prime envelope falls below 4; induction on Omega=1,...,8 makes every proper prefix below 4 and ensures termination. The standard-library exact Fraction program visits 1,1,1,1,1,3,8,33 nodes at total multiplicities 1..8 and exactly five rationally verified leaves; checked explicit divisor-partition certificates cover every divisor once with sums sigma(n)/4. A separately implemented finite sieve to n<=300000 agrees but is not the global proof. No probabilistic or floating-point assumptions.

value.rationale: The smallest feasible total prime-factor multiplicity is a natural structural invariant, different from the known smallest numerical four-layered integer. Closing its complete five-element equality fiber with explicit four-way divisor certificates provides a motivated first layer, not an arbitrary cutoff. The strict-inequality instances add information absent from quadriperfect equality classifications; 235620 lies outside the initial A204831 display. The proof unifies an unbounded-prime bound with exact finite factorization/partition certificates; no downstream theorem is claimed or required.
